findings.title: Studio launcher never produces control/method.json: _replay sends the whole reply list in one call, which the card refuses
findings.detail: shared-bridge/studio_bridge.py:1138-1141 builds ONE argv carrying every reply (--reply r1 --reply r2 ...) and never first primes a pending question. scripts/core/choice_card/intake_card/intake_session.py:495-501 refuses any turn whose reply list has more than one unrecorded entry (len(new) > 1 -> ONE_REPLY_AT_A_TIME, outcome waiting, rc 2), and :480 refuses replies when no question was presented yet in this session (QUESTION_NOT_PRESENTED). The bridge treats any nonzero rc as REPLAY_FAILED and returns before printing the poll line (studio_bridge.py:1301-1302), so a NEW Studio order never reaches the wake/next step and no method record is ever written.
findings.observed: 3/3 replay attempts EXIT 1 REPLAY_FAILED; control/method.json absent after each; poll would return error before emitting the run line
findings.expected_by_acceptance: control/method.json present and the run inside the upgraded strategy after a new Studio order
findings.attribution: PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by this unit: the same bulk replay also fails against factory.py reverted to pre-fix 4097da395 (legacy reply list: EXIT 1, no method record). The unit's own test block [3] asserts the refusal path only ('no method record claimed without accepted replies'), so it does not prove E1c.

findings.title: Existing legacy-shaped Studio orders are now cancelled instead of retried
findings.detail: studio_bridge._question_mismatch counts replies against the card with purpose_flow=True unconditionally (shared-bridge/studio_bridge.py:1090). A legacy-shaped 15-reply order now returns (2, 16) and _refuse_mismatch cancels it at the studio with REPLAY_QUESTION_MISMATCH. A purpose-shaped 18-reply order passes the guard (None) and then dies on F1. Reported as context for F1; not counted as a separate acceptance failure because the same bulk-replay refusal already blocked those orders.
findings.attribution: The guard lives in shared-bridge (no owner in the plan). Whether the guard was purpose_flow=True before this unit was not established; no blame assigned.

findings.title: Purpose default is read from the run directory, so every launcher that reaches factory.py card inherits it
findings.detail: factory.py:2930 _purpose_flow_for: an explicit flag wins; else control/method.json, control/studio-order.json, a saved PURPOSE answer, or a run with no progress files -> purpose card; a run with no run dir or with recorded progress -> keeps the card it had. _run_is_new returns False on an unreadable store, so a broken store preserves rather than reshapes. This is what makes E2 hold. Not a defect; recorded so the decision surface is auditable.
